method: Manual adjudication of 30 of the 121 disagreements between Apertus' source level and the label set from archival evidence (10 random per group, seed 7). Each record judged from its title, date, scope and archive hierarchy.

items.note: Mixed administrative dossier (legal questions, correspondence) that also contains clippings.
Clippings collected by the Alcohol Administration for monitoring: journalism (secondary) kept as an administrative record (primary).
Press clippings on the 1939 national exhibition.
Obituaries: biographical synthesis after the fact.
Reception of delegates: correspondence and lists. Apertus said tertiary, label said secondary.
Printed matter and clippings; Apertus called it tertiary.
Drafts of press releases written by the library itself.
Administrative file of a 1978 reform (reports, conference, clippings).
A 1902 newspaper article: contemporary report (primary for historians) or second-hand account (secondary).
Petitions plus printed material: the petitions are primary.

Commission minutes (primary) with a report on the history of flour imports (secondary part).
